image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) standing on a paved surface in front of a red brick wall. The duck on the left is viewed from the rear-left, showing its grey body, white tail feathers, and orange webbed feet. The duck on the right is viewed from the front-right, displaying its characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, brown chest, and grey body. Both appear to be walking or standing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right clearly displays a broad, flat, yellowish-green bill typical of a mallard drake.
The visible eye of the right duck is small and dark, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the classic robust, oval-shaped body structure of a mallard with smooth, dense-looking feather texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject on the right perfectly matches the male mallard description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, brown chest, and grey flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The feet of both ducks are visible. They are orange, positioned posteriorly, and show clear webbing between the toes. The anatomy appears structurally sound.
The folded wings on the left duck show the correct layering and shape, tapering towards the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left duck shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (sex feathers) typical of male mallards.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or generic 'duck' classifications.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra digits, which are common AI artifacts in waterfowl.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex feather textures and the background, especially around the head and tail.
To assess overall sharpness and look for subtle texture anomalies in the pavement or brickwork that might indicate generation issues.
To ensure the ducks are properly grounded on the pavement and not floating, and that the depth relationship with the wall is correct.

focus_areas: Webbed foot anatomy (toe count and webbing connectivity)
Feather texture consistency (especially the transition from green head to white neck ring)
Contact shadows between feet and pavement
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the feet of the left duck; AI often struggles with the angle of the foot when viewed from behind. Verify if the webbing looks like a solid membrane or if it has unnatural holes/fusion. Check the reflection/shadows on the wet-looking pavement for consistency with the light source.
